body.statement: Construct one total test that, using the lexicographically first minimizer in \(\mathcal K_n\), has rejection probability at most \(a_0\) uniformly on \(\mathcal H_0\) for every \(n\), type-II error at most \(b_0\) whenever \(D(P)\ge C r_{\mathrm{test}}(n)\), deterministic tuning, and stated arithmetic and memory costs through dense and sparse occupancy regimes. A valid target cost is \(O(|\mathcal K_n|n+\sum_{\mathbf k\in\mathcal K_n}R(\mathbf k))\) arithmetic and \(O(\max_{\mathbf k\in\mathcal K_n}R(\mathbf k))\) memory, with any sharper certified implementation recorded. Next prove \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}(n)\asymp r_{\mathrm{test}}(n)\) with constants depending only on \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\). Only after that equivalence is established, denote their common order by \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}(n;\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L)\), simplify it in every regime including equality-case logarithms, and conclude \(\rho_n^*\asymp r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\). If the two deterministic optimizations do not match, state the remaining upper--lower gap instead of defining a common rate.
body.justification: The theorem-level kernel is still the construction and matching of independently evaluable repaired upper and lower procedures on the identical class. The exact likelihood audit and corrected first-projection inequality delimit those procedures but do not substitute for them.
body.gap: CrumpHotzImbensMitnik2008 and the other direct CATE-homogeneity comparators do not supply a uniform fixed-sample three-index H"older radius. Conditional-independence and doubly robust functional results provide relevant techniques, but no frozen cited theorem supplies the required two-scale exact-uniform null mixture together with a matching profiled sparse-occupancy test. The remaining gap is therefore the explicit paired construction, not optimization of the disproved frozen envelopes.
body.consumer: Once completed, the result would supply a detectability benchmark and an omnibus procedure for causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows without certifying a fitted forest; the present bracket and no-penalty region provide only partial benchmarks.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a two-scale, exact-uniform, null-componentwise constant-CATE pair of priors whose unavoidable degree-two predictive discrepancy is bounded at the optimal scale, and construct the matching multiresolution corrected-energy test with all sparse-occupancy Hoeffding projections controlled. Then optimize both independently and prove their equivalence in every \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d\) regime, including transition logarithms.
obligation.obstruction: The exact binary likelihood calculation shows that positive induced CATE amplitude equals a difference of nuisance cross-moments. The coefficient of \(B(x_i)B(x_j)\) in the two-observation prior-predictive product then cannot vanish: cancelling it for all four binary rows forces equality of the full second-moment matrices and hence zero CATE amplitude. Thus the lower envelope must pay an order-two term \((n)_2M^{-d}\delta^2\). At \(d=\gamma=1\) and \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), a one-scale construction is additionally limited by CATE smoothness from using the rough product amplitude; a legal sharp construction must aggregate micro-scale nuisance cross-moments into a macro-scale Lipschitz effect. On the upper side, the corrected signal-dependent first projection removes the frozen \(n^{-1/4}\) distance floor, but the frozen core supplies no multiresolution covariance-correction kernel from which the ranks and the order-two through order-four sparse-occupancy variances can be derived. Those two missing constructions are precisely the novel kernel and cannot be assumed.
obligation.attempted: I wrote the null and alternative four-cell probability maps, divided them by a common interior law to obtain the exact one-observation likelihood ratios, expanded the full prior-predictive product with every power of \(q_\tau=4\delta\), and computed the first nonmatching two-observation coefficient. I also solved the first-projection quadratic variance inequality and stress-tested the resulting mandatory degree-two term at \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,9/10)\). This removes the old \(n^{-5/14}\) contradiction but does not manufacture the missing two-scale prior or corrected multiresolution statistic.
obligation.partial_result:
The following calculation repairs the first defective likelihood order, but it also isolates why the complete theorem is not yet proved.  Work in one lattice cell and let \(B:\mathcal X\to[0,1]\) be its collar bump.  Use as dominating conditional law the interior law \(P_\star\) with
\[
 e_\star=\frac12,\qquad m_{0,\star}=\frac38,\qquad \tau_\star=\frac18.
\]
In the order \((a,y)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), its four conditional cell probabilities are
\[
 (p_{00}^\star,p_{01}^\star,p_{10}^\star,p_{11}^\star)
 =\left(\frac5{16},\frac3{16},\frac14,\frac14\right),
\]
so every likelihood ratio below is well defined.  Let \(\nu_0\) and \(\nu_1\) be bounded laws for a pair \((U,V)\), each having \(\mathbb E U=\mathbb E V=0\), and put
\[
 \delta=\mathbb E_{\nu_0}(UV)-\mathbb E_{\nu_1}(UV)>0.
\]
For a null component indexed by \((U,V)\sim\nu_0\), set
\[
 e_0=\frac12+UB,\qquad m_{0,0}=\frac38+VB,
 \qquad \tau_0\equiv\frac18.
\]
For an alternative component indexed by \((U,V)\sim\nu_1\), set
\[
 e_1=\frac12+UB,\qquad
 m_{0,1}=\frac38+VB-2\delta B^2,
 \qquad \tau_1=\frac18+4\delta B^2.                       \tag{A}
\]
Bounds such as \(|U|+|V|+4\delta\le1/16\) are sufficient for all four Bernoulli probabilities to remain in the prescribed interior box; the actual H\"older restrictions additionally constrain the support radii after rescaling the bump.  Direct multiplication gives the full null conditional probability map
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
(a,y)&p^0_{ay}(x;U,V)\\ \hline
(0,0)&\displaystyle \frac5{16}-\left(\frac{5U}{8}+\frac V2\right)B+UVB^2\\
(0,1)&\displaystyle \frac3{16}+\left(-\frac{3U}{8}+\frac V2\right)B-UVB^2\\
(1,0)&\displaystyle \frac14+\frac{U-V}{2}B-UVB^2\\
(1,1)&\displaystyle \frac14+\frac{U+V}{2}B+UVB^2,
\end{array}                                                     \tag{B}
\]
and the full alternative map is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
(a,y)&p^1_{ay}(x;U,V)\\ \hline
(0,0)&p^0_{00}(x;U,V)+\delta B^2-2\delta UB^3\\
(0,1)&p^0_{01}(x;U,V)-\delta B^2+2\delta UB^3\\
(1,0)&p^0_{10}(x;U,V)-\delta B^2-2\delta UB^3\\
(1,1)&p^0_{11}(x;U,V)+\delta B^2+2\delta UB^3.
\end{array}                                                     \tag{C}
\]
The rows in each display sum to one.  Moreover, (B)--(C) are exactly the four products \((1-e)(1-m_0)\), \((1-e)m_0\), \(e(1-m_0-\tau)\), and \(e(m_0+\tau)\), so they are binary cell probabilities for the regressions in (A), rather than merely a formal likelihood perturbation.

For \(s=(a,y)\), define the row vectors and scalar coefficients
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
s&r_s=(r_{s,U},r_{s,V})&k_s&j_s\\ \hline
(0,0)&(-2,-8/5)&16/5&-32/5\\
(0,1)&(-2, 8/3)&-16/3&32/3\\
(1,0)&( 2,-2)&-4&-8\\
(1,1)&( 2, 2)&4&8.
\end{array}                                                     \tag{D}
\]
Dividing (B)--(C) by \(p_s^\star\) gives the one-observation likelihood ratios
\[
 L_s^0(U,V;x)=1+\{r_s\mathbin{\cdot}(U,V)\}B(x)+k_sUVB(x)^2, \tag{E}
\]
\[
 L_s^1(U,V;x)=1+\{r_s\mathbin{\cdot}(U,V)\}B(x)
   +k_s\{UV+\delta\}B(x)^2+j_s\delta U B(x)^3.            \tag{F}
\]
Here \(r_s\mathbin{\cdot}(U,V)=r_{s,U}U+r_{s,V}V\).  Taking expectations in (E)--(F), using the two zero-mean restrictions and the definition of \(\delta\), proves exact equality of the one-observation prior predictive laws.

The complete fixed-sample expansion also shows every coefficient involving the CATE amplitude.  Put
\[
 N_i(U,V)=1+\{r_{s_i}\mathbin{\cdot}(U,V)\}B_i+k_{s_i}UVB_i^2,
 \qquad C_i(U)=k_{s_i}B_i^2+j_{s_i}UB_i^3,
\]
where \(B_i=B(x_i)\).  Since the nonconstant CATE amplitude in (A) is \(q_\tau=4\delta\), for every \(r\ge1\),
\[
 \overline L_{0,r}=\mathbb E_{\nu_0}\prod_{i=1}^rN_i(U,V),           \tag{G}
\]
whereas
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \overline L_{1,r}
 &=\mathbb E_{\nu_1}\prod_{i=1}^r
       \left\{N_i(U,V)+\frac{q_\tau}{4}C_i(U)\right\}\\
 &=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}}
   \left(\frac{q_\tau}{4}\right)^{|S|}
   \mathbb E_{\nu_1}\left[
      \prod_{i\in S}C_i(U)\prod_{i\notin S}N_i(U,V)
   \right].                                                       \tag{H}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus (H), including all powers \((q_\tau/4)^{|S|}\) and their coefficients, is the exact prior-predictive product; there is no unexpanded remainder in the CATE amplitude.

The first unavoidable mismatch occurs at two observations.  The coefficient of \(B_iB_k\) in \(\overline L_{0,2}-\overline L_{1,2}\) is
\[
 r_{s_i}(\Sigma_0-\Sigma_1)r_{s_k}^{\top},
 \qquad
 \Sigma_j=\mathbb E_{\nu_j}
 \begin{pmatrix}U\\V\end{pmatrix}
 \begin{pmatrix}U&V\end{pmatrix}.                                \tag{I}
\]
Neither the \(q_\tau B_i^2\) term nor the \(q_\tau UB_i^3\) term in (F) contributes to the distinct monomial \(B_iB_k\).  The vectors \(r_{(1,1)}=(2,2)^\top\) and \(r_{(1,0)}=(2,-2)^\top\) form a basis of \(\mathbb R^2\).  Hence vanishing of (I) for all two-observation binary rows forces \(\Sigma_0=\Sigma_1\).  Its off-diagonal entry would then give \(\mathbb E_{\nu_0}(UV)=\mathbb E_{\nu_1}(UV)\), contradicting \(\delta>0\).  Therefore a positive-separation null-supported construction cannot cancel its degree-two predictive coefficient.  Any valid divergence envelope must contain a term of order
\[
 (n)_2 M^{-d}\delta^2,                                            \tag{J}
\]
up to fixed constants and support-controlled higher terms.  This proves directly that the legal path with no nuisance amplitude and \(q_\tau>0\) cannot be assigned only a tenth-power remainder.

The stress test requested in the directive now behaves correctly.  At \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,9/10)\), a one-scale null construction has \(\delta\lesssim h^{\alpha+\beta}=h\) by the two nuisance H\"older bounds.  Combining this with (J) gives \(n^2h\delta^2\lesssim1\), whose balanced scale is \(h\asymp n^{-2/3}\) and \(\delta\asymp n^{-2/3}\).  This is smaller than the established oracle obstruction \(n^{-2/5}\), so the spurious \(n^{-5/14}\) lower obstruction cannot recur after the degree-two term is charged.

The upper-side first projection can likewise be corrected without imposing an unconditional \(n^{-1/2}\) energy floor.  For the frozen fourth-order single-scale kernel, let
\[
 q_h=\min_{c\in I}Q_h(c),\qquad
 V_{n,J}=\frac{J}{n^2}+\frac{J^2}{n^3}+\frac{J^3}{n^4}.
\]
Its first canonical projection has squared norm at most a fixed multiple of \(q_h\); the remaining three projections have total variance at most a fixed multiple of \(V_{n,J}\).  Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\{U_h(c_\star)\}
 \le C\left(\frac{q_h}{n}+V_{n,J}\right),                         \tag{K}
\]
where \(c_\star\) minimizes the population quadratic.  If the null approximation has magnitude at most \(B_h\), uniform one-sided Chebyshev bounds reduce the power requirement to
\[
 q_h\ge C_1\left{B_h^2+\sqrt{V_{n,J}}+sqrt{q_h/n}\right}.        \tag{L}
\]
Writing \(x=\sqrt{q_h}\) and using \(C_1x/\sqrt n\le x^2/2+C_1^2/(2n)\), a sufficient explicit solution of (L) is
\[
 x\ge C_2\left\{B_h+V_{n,J}^{1/4}+n^{-1/2}\right\}.               \tag{M}
\]
Thus the first-projection contribution is of order \(n^{-1/2}\) on the distance scale, not \(n^{-1/4}\).  Formula (M) explains both the validity of the established single-scale upper bound and the failure of the frozen rank-free term in \(U_n\).

Combining the already proved known-propensity converse with the already proved single-scale test gives the rigorous all-regime bracket.  With \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), for constants depending only on the fixed class parameters and all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\le\rho_n^*\le C
 \begin{cases}
 n^{-2t/(4t+d)},&d\le4t,\\
 n^{-4t/(4t+3d)},&d>4t.
 \end{cases}                                                       \tag{N}
\]
When \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\) and \(d\le4\gamma\), the two sides of (N) agree and give \(\rho_n^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\); at \(d=4\gamma\) this argument gives \(n^{-1/4}\) with no logarithm.

What remains is not an algebraic optimization of the frozen handles.  At the early-kill point \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), a one-scale product perturbation is limited by CATE smoothness to \(\delta\lesssim h\), even though the two nuisance amplitudes can have product of order \(h^{1/5}\).  Achieving the latter amplitude while preserving a Lipschitz CATE requires a genuine two-scale construction whose micro-cell cross-moment field aggregates into a smooth macro-scale function.  On the upper side, the matching operation is an explicit multiresolution estimator of the within-signal-cell nuisance covariance with all of its order-two through order-four projections controlled in sparse occupancy.  Neither construction, nor a theorem identifying their two finite optimizations in every regime, follows from the frozen primitives.  Therefore the exact all-regime radius and any transition logarithms remain open, and \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) cannot yet be defined.
